headline: High: Airbyte’s broad egress plus Great Expectations’ file-based validation can create default data-leak and cascading-error paths; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte exposes an API and broad network egress, while Great Expectations reads files for data sources, validation results, and documentation. That creates a plausible manual or file-based bridge where content from one can influence the other, but no shared channel or parser is documented, so the pathway is limited and uncertain.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs are copied into files that Great Expectations parses as configuration or documentation, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace or clipboard, content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Keep Airbyte outputs and Great Expectations configs in separate directories.
Review any copied text before pasting it into Great Expectations files.
Disable automatic ingestion of generated docs as executable config.
Use read-only exports for Airbyte artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the two tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and touches business data; Great Expectations reads and writes validation artifacts and documentation. If they share a workspace, Airbyte can move business data into files that Great Expectations later processes, creating a default leakage path from sensitive data into validation outputs or logs.
conditions: IF Airbyte writes business data into a shared directory, Great Expectations can read it.
IF Great Expectations stores validation results in the same workspace, sensitive fields may be duplicated into artifacts.
mitigations: Separate source-data and validation-artifact directories.
Restrict Airbyte connectors to non-sensitive datasets for shared runs.
Turn off verbose validation logging.
Delete temporary files after each run.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation with per-tool mounts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can make outbound API calls and Great Expectations can install packages and manipulate files. Even without explicit write permissions listed for Airbyte, both can affect the same data-engineering workspace, so overlapping mutable-state operations are plausible and could clobber artifacts or dependency state.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same project directory, file and dependency state can conflict.
IF Airbyte writes generated artifacts while Great Expectations installs or updates packages, runs may interfere.
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate virtual environment.
Pin package versions before executing Great Expectations.
Use distinct output directories for each tool.
Serialize runs so only one agent mutates the workspace at a time.
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations commonly consumes data sources and validation results, so Airbyte-produced outputs can become its inputs. Because Airbyte can emit data over the network and Great Expectations can treat files as authoritative validation material, an upstream mistake can cascade into incorrect tests or documentation unless explicitly checked.
conditions: IF Great Expectations is pointed at Airbyte-generated files, it may validate bad upstream data as if it were ground truth.
IF downstream reports are generated from those validations, the error propagates to documentation or decisions.
mitigations: Add a manual review step before using Airbyte outputs as test fixtures.
Compare validation results against an independent sample.
Mark generated files clearly as untrusted inputs.
Limit downstream automation to non-production datasets.
requires-engineering: add schema and freshness checks between the tools.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only business data / validation artifacts are listed, so there is no direct residency or regulated-data mismatch evidenced here. Airbyte’s broad egress and Great Expectations’ file handling still create a small compliance gap if sensitive business data is placed into shared artifacts, but the pairwise evidence is limited.
conditions: IF regulated data is loaded into Airbyte and then written into Great Expectations artifacts, retention and residency controls may diverge.
IF the workspace is shared across jurisdictions, artifact storage location becomes relevant.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared validation runs.
Set short retention on validation artifacts.
Document where Airbyte outputs are stored.
Review whether any dataset is subject to special handling.
requires-engineering: implement jurisdiction-aware storage controls.
